REVIEWER B — E07 ROUND4 SOURCE REVIEW

Verdict: PASS, source-only. Total meaningful assessments: 84. Classified findings: must-fix 0, should-fix 0, consider 0. Score: 100 × (84 − 0 − 0) / 84 = 100. No evidence-backed, patch-introduced defect meeting the required ≥9/10 finding-confidence threshold was identified. This is one independent source verdict, not the dual-review AND result, a runtime verification, or authorization to mark stories accepted.

REVIEW METHOD AND BOUNDARIES
Read the complete round4 brief, project conventions, scope, epic plan, all six story specifications and task lists, audit, repair response, and all six historical round1–3 reports. Reviewed the implementation manifest and relevant consuming-side routing, authority admission, persistence, renderer, parser, and deterministic-peer test boundaries. Historical failed reviews were treated as repair obligations, not approval. The source base/branch are parent-supplied manifest information; no Git command or independent baseline diff was performed because the assignment expressly forbids Git. No edits, saved artifacts, builds, tests, lint, formatting, provider/network/auth operations, or process/global mutations were performed. No current Reviewer A report was inspected and no contact was made.

PER-STORY COVERAGE AND ASSESSMENTS
Each numbered item below is a source assessment, not an independently executed acceptance result.

E07S01 — Modal Menu and native-safe mode entry: 12 assessments, no findings.
01. src/projects.rs config validation and src/tui.rs mode-key construction agree on F1–F24/none, with a missing old-daemon setting retaining the documented F12 default.
02. Invalid mode-key configuration is rejected through the existing validated persistence path rather than publishing a partially changed configuration.
03. src/tui.rs reserves the configured mode key and legacy prefix without converting ordinary native Escape, j, or k into global navigation commands.
04. src/tui/menu.rs represents navigation and literal search separately; slash enters search, while search letters are not reinterpreted as Menu commands.
05. Menu paste is consumed instead of executed as a sequence of navigation commands; literal editing remains confined to explicit search/form contexts.
06. key_bytes and is_prefix consistently support explicit F13–F24 and exact shifted-lower aliases, preserving additional modifier distinctions and terminfo forwarding bytes.
07. The documented legacy Shift-F3/F15 cursor-reply ambiguity agrees with the actual parser dispatch; the implementation does not claim that ambiguous legacy input is solved.
08. Deliberate double-mode-key forwarding requires Press semantics and the immediate pending gesture; reported Repeat/Release is not counted as a new deliberate confirmation.
09. Double-key and Actions forwarding enter NativeControl's existing authority-gated input path rather than bypassing current target/control checks.
10. Escape/i return from Menu without replaying intercepted input or resetting the managed native process; canvas clearing is client presentation work only.
11. Parent routing gives ownership warnings/panels precedence over Menu and dialog actions, preventing covered input from becoming later application input.
12. Keyboard and mouse Menu selection operate on the same current native/ACP rows; row traversal and hierarchy handling have explicit malformed-cycle protection.

E07S02 — Conversation-first ACP and explicit interaction cards: 16 assessments, no findings.
13. src/tui/agent.rs prioritizes conversation and active interaction controls; diagnostic settings/history are separately read-only, wrapped, scrollable panes.
14. Canonical event ingestion is sequence-aware and bounded, records gaps/eviction, and does not infer conversation completion or callback answers from rendered text.
15. Genuine form cards retain interaction identity/revision and supported typed values; local Review does not itself submit a response or manufacture default consent.
16. Submit captures the reviewed values and original authority envelope; subsequent field editing clears that captured review rather than silently submitting an old or changed draft.
17. Permission requests expose exact broker-offered option IDs. The broker validates that selected ID against the original pending interaction and replies on its retained wire RPC.
18. Short/narrow permission layouts wrap and follow focused choices; oversized unselected choices first reveal context and require a fresh painted activation.
19. Mutation actions use immutable painted provenance and presentation → conclusive Empty → armed repaint. New/replaced permissions, authentication, foreground interruption, decline, cancel, and reviewed Submit are covered.
20. Compatibility F5/F6/F7, Ctrl-C, focused Enter/Space, and mouse activation converge on painted admission rather than an independent shortcut bypass.
21. Parent after_draw admission follows a successful draw and exact InputReadiness::Empty; Pending/Inconclusive cannot arm consent, and covered ACP panes are excluded.
22. Geometry changes, clipping, help, hidden surfaces, target/grant changes, and relevant interaction revisions invalidate readiness instead of promoting old queued gestures.
23. Stable same-target prompt paste followed by Enter and the first local Review remain immediate; the fix does not impose blanket double confirmation on ordinary editing.
24. Authentication consumes the actual broker method_id/kind projection. Exact inert IDs and support context are displayed, while unsupported client/terminal methods cannot dispatch authentication.
25. Authentication keyboard and mouse actions capture their own method ID; selecting an alternate mouse button does not reuse the previously highlighted method.
26. Authentication dispatch reaches the broker's explicit offered-agent-method validation and original authenticate request; there is no inferred name field, terminal-login fallback, or automatic retry.
27. First null-to-established session transition on the same instance/connection preserves read-only Details/History but discards authority-bound mutation state; true replacement still resets identity-dependent state.
28. Definite unadmitted answer/permission rejection restoration checks the captured binding and interaction revision, restores editable state locally, and never automatically replays a mutation.

E07S03 — Safe close and identifiable sessions: 10 assessments, no findings.
29. src/tui/menu.rs close dialogs capture the selected native ID or exact ACP tuple/control/generation rather than resolving a later selection when confirmation arrives.
30. Live close defaults to Keep working. Close consent requires the complete captured presentation and input-empty boundary; resize/help invalidate presentation and Repeat cannot confirm.
31. Close, Detach UI, and exited-record removal are distinct actions; choosing Keep or detaching is not a hidden peer/process close.
32. ACP close is routed through NativeControl's ACP worker and the daemon's original authority/broker admission, not borrowed from a newly acquired grant.
33. Native exited-record removal still checks actual liveness in the daemon and does not erase a live process record as a presentation shortcut.
34. Exact native/ACP rename reaches the existing name operation; ACP rename updates the descriptor without starting another peer, changing its tuple, or completing retained work.
35. Rename editing rejects unsafe or oversized whole edits rather than silently submitting a truncated or stale displayed identity.
36. preferred_view and has_views consider both native and ACP views; removing the final native does not turn surviving ACP work into an empty-window/new-shell workflow.
37. The real last-native regression source normally exits/removes its shell, reopens the surviving ACP row, and asserts the original question/RPC/peer/generation and one arithmetic57 effect without a replacement shell.
38. Session rows and headers distinguish native/ACP type, useful name, status, and leaf-preserving paths; identification changes do not alter backend ownership semantics.

E07S04 — Visible creation and explicit placement: 12 assessments, no findings.
39. Menu New captures its source and exposes native versus ACP plus current versus independent placement; parent routing consumes both choices explicitly.
40. The New dispatcher checks project_save_terminal:true before native open and before ACP catalog/dialog entry. Missing/false capability produces a local refusal without a misleading old-placement fallback.
41. A disappeared captured source is refused rather than substituted with the main shell or another current session.
42. Native independent placement creates a distinct runtime project while retaining captured cwd/export semantics; inherited hooks/recipes are not copied into that independent project.
43. ACP independent placement is propagated through the launch request and daemon consumer, which validates the existing canonical directory and does not create project directories.
44. ACP launch selects trusted bounded profile argv and explicit structured settings; it does not assemble a shell command from profile labels or user-entered settings.
45. Automatic launch names reserve the suffix within the backend's128-byte UTF8 bound and retreat to a character boundary; explicit names are rejected rather than truncated.
46. Basic and Advanced launcher fields preserve exact project/profile/model/mode/effort/options identities; legal JSON whitespace and inherited profile options are not converted into guessed settings.
47. While launch is pending, the retained dialog is frozen; a typed definite DaemonError restores the same full draft and cause, while ambiguous transport failure does not become an automatic retry.
48. Parsed successful launch identity is captured for recovery before a subsequent fallible snapshot/observation, including the worker teardown receipt path.
49. Launch errors remain accessible through wrapping/scrollable form and contextual Help, including the full server cause rather than only a shortened banner.
50. The owned-wrapper rejection regression source verifies no peer/project side effect at refusal, unchanged Advanced fields, no retry after executable restoration, and one fresh explicit successful launch/effect42.

E07S05 — Structured project editing and authoritative save preview: 12 assessments, no findings.
51. src/tui/project.rs separates project name, ordered hook source/timeout, and recipe name/command controls; raw JSON is not required for approved editing operations.
52. Nested editors mutate only a local draft on acceptance; nested cancel preserves unrelated values and outer cancellation does not send a partial patch.
53. Hook order and timeouts are retained, recipe rename checks collisions before removing the old key, and whole-field rejection remains blocking until deliberate correction.
54. Apply submits a complete validated patch; definite persistence errors retain the draft for an explicit corrected attempt instead of partially applying UI changes.
55. Save stores the captured native or ACP source ID and submits that exact terminal selector together with project and expected_context; the round1 ACP-main-shell fallback is removed.
56. Preview and Save share daemon project_save_source/context resolution, reject project/source mismatch, and use the selected ACP launch cwd or native captured cwd rather than a different session's context.
57. Directory/Git-root resolution occurs outside the topology lock, followed by source/context revalidation before persistent mutation; intervening context drift is rejected.
58. The persistence candidate is validated before store publication and uses the existing conflict-aware atomic write path, preserving stable project IDs and the configuration/runtime separation.
59. Serialized project-open retains its reservation while inspecting live ACP metadata outside topology; starting/auth-required/ready ACP-only projects reuse the original view without creating shells or running open hooks.
60. Ended/failed ACP metadata does not indefinitely suppress an ordinary fresh shell/open-hook path; this opposite branch has an actual backend consumer regression.
61. Forget defaults to cancellation and removes saved metadata only; it does not delete directories, terminate sessions, or cancel already admitted work.
62. CLI hierarchy/request routing and README distinguish projects add/save/open/config/remove from terminal removal and retain the documented CLI default-main save behavior without claiming selected-session semantics for an omitted selector.

E07S06 — Consistent controls and truthful attention/status: 10 assessments, no findings.
63. Shared responsive action_buttons produces the same visible rectangles used for hit testing, with side-by-side, stacked, and compact layouts rather than unrelated mouse geometry.
64. Tab/BackTab, mouse, explicit Help, and Escape are handled within the active form/pane; literal j/k/? in text fields are not stolen for global navigation.
65. Contextual Help wraps and scrolls, carries full inert last-action/error context, and returns to the same local draft instead of replaying covered editing input.
66. Full dialog failures have reachable contextual presentation, addressing the round1 clipped-error defect without suppressing the underlying error or discarding its draft.
67. ACP attention is derived from canonical pending-unsubmitted interactions, foreground work, outcome, and lifecycle, rather than guessing from terminal output or copied labels.
68. Broker attention metadata is explicitly forwarded by daemon snapshots and consumed by native/ACP row/header rendering; the new value is not silently discarded at a module boundary.
69. Question/permission attention stops counting submitted selections while canonical completed records remain available for inspection; it does not imply protocol completion from a local click alone.
70. Normal native exit displays the real exit status and appropriate Close/New controls instead of an ownership-resynchronization alarm.
71. Empty-window rendering and keyboard/mouse actions use combined native/ACP availability, consistently with replacement selection and project-open consumers.
72. NativeSurface damage caching and the Menu-to-session canvas refresh preserve client rendering/background state without clearing managed application state or resending application input.

CROSS-CUTTING AUTHORITY, SECURITY, TEST QUALITY, PERFORMANCE, AND MAINTAINABILITY: 12 assessments, no findings.
73. Producer-to-consumer tracing covered Menu actions, dialog submissions, asynchronous launch receipts/rejections, ACP operation variants, attention metadata, and project placement/save fields; each relevant value has a functioning receiving branch.
74. Daemon ACP admission still binds exact target/instance/connection/session, controller, generation, and unique call_id before broker commit; stale or duplicate operations do not become new grants or retargeted work.
75. NativeControl retains the original bounded FIFO worker and existing typed dialog/result patterns. The patch does not introduce a second transport/authority abstraction; no concrete introduced Fowler smell requiring a finding was supported.
76. Ordinary Owner Yield/Release capture the original grant Arc identity, generation, observed owner, and exact manual claim. All keyboard/focus/mouse routes require complete presentation, Empty, and unchanged Armed repaint; changed or transiently replaced facts invalidate consent, and Repeat is consumed.
77. Owner Keep/Return remain local. Force does not implicitly interrupt/kill; pending ordinary cancellation targets its captured claim and grants nobody; conditional Keep remains ordered on the original FIFO before subsequent application activity.
78. Untrusted ACP text, IDs, options, errors, control characters, and bidi formatting are rendered inert with explicit local bounds. Ordinary snapshots/events remain metadata-only; content inspection remains explicit, bounded, and gap-aware.
79. Trusted ACP profiles use bounded argv without shell interpolation; intentional user-configured hooks retain the separately documented /bin/sh -c contract and bounded timeout rather than disguising shell execution as profile data.
80. Authentication tests use actual broker method_id/kind projection and exact retained wire requests. The readiness helper compares desired and inactive styles against the truly inactive Details action, avoiding the prior symmetric inverse-highlight false positive.
81. Stopped-real-TUI F5/permission/Owner tests queue physical input before state transitions and use subsequent Details plus original-connection receipts to prove consumption; they assert unchanged authority, original RPC/PID, no premature effect, then one fresh deliberate effect.
82. Test sources retain bounded waits, owned private fixtures, termios restoration, reader joins, normal shutdown and peer identity/effect assertions. FIRST evaluation is risk-proportionate: deterministic local integration tests exercise real boundaries; ignored provider consumers are not represented as fresh runtime evidence.
83. wrap_rows restricts byte/cell arithmetic to printable ASCII lines, preserves byte-range output without an extra String copy, and retains grapheme-width handling and cross-line accounting for other content. Exact-width, trailing-newline, blank, emoji, and combining-mark source tests cover the permanent semantic boundary.
84. Retained Details/history row layouts remain cached and bounded; the optimization does not reduce retained context, raise capacity/timeouts, or alter recovery policy. Added recovery failure excerpts are test-only, bounded, and escaped; they are diagnostics, not proof of bg408's initiating cause.

PRIOR-REPAIR DISPOSITION
Round1: checked exact ACP Save, painted compatibility submit identity, automatic Unicode naming, full errors, short permission options, and the superseding upper-key repair. Round2: checked generalized mutation fencing, retained definite launch rejection, serialized ACP-only project reuse, final-native removal selection, and explicit/shifted upper-key recognition. Round3: checked capability admission before either New branch; immutable ordinary Owner consent across grant/request/presentation changes; real auth identities and unsupported no-effect behavior; same-instance initial session establishment; and the corrected auth test readiness predicate. No historical finding was waived or counted as approval. Current classifications remain zero findings.
